guide_enrichment.narrative:
We see very little separation between our longer-run expectation and what the market is pricing. Our strongest matchup signal favors Missouri’s defense, particularly its ability to prevent opponents from creating scoring opportunities. We also recognize the uncertainty behind that advantage: Missouri returned only two defensive starters and lost 10 from last season’s unit. Holding Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 198 total yards was encouraging, but we are not treating one opener as proof that the rebuilt group will match last year’s level.

We have a similar question on the other side of the ball. Austin Simmons completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards and four touchdowns in his Missouri debut, but our underlying passing numbers remain less convincing than that performance. We think Mississippi State’s pass defense can provide a more meaningful test for an offense working with a new starting quarterback, a first-year offensive coordinator and several changes up front.

For us, those competing signals explain why the market and our model land in nearly the same place. Missouri has the more favorable defensive matchup in our numbers, but the personnel turnover and uncertainty around the passing offense keep us from finding enough value at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Mississippi State’s offense against Missouri’s scoring-opportunity defense. Our numbers suggest Missouri can limit the Bulldogs’ ability to turn drives into serious scoring threats, and the Tigers held their opening opponent to 13 first downs and 3-of-13 on third down. The question for us is whether that prevention travels against a stronger test despite the extensive defensive turnover. If it does, Missouri has a clearer path to controlling the game; if it does not, the market’s resistance to pricing a wider gap makes sense.

recent_game.fact: Missouri opened the 2026 season with a 54-14 victory over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Sept. 3.
Missouri produced 562 total yards against Arkansas-Pine Bluff, including 357 passing and 205 rushing, while allowing 198 total yards.
Missouri led Arkansas-Pine Bluff 40-0 at halftime and held a 376-6 advantage in first-half yardage.
Missouri converted 6 of 10 third downs, both fourth-down attempts and all five red-zone opportunities in the opener.

quarterback.fact: Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons is listed as Missouri's starting quarterback, with sophomore Matt Zollers as the backup.
In his Missouri debut, Simmons completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Simmons' 89.5% completion rate and 270.4 passer rating were the highest by a quarterback in a Missouri debut.
Simmons is the seventh different starting quarterback of the Eli Drinkwitz era and the third transfer quarterback to start during that span.
Zollers completed 8 of 12 passes for 87 yards and scored his first collegiate rushing touchdown in the season opener.

offensive_personnel.fact: Missouri's listed starting offensive line is LT Cayden Green, LG Tristan Wilson, C Dominick Giudice, RG Curtis Peagler and RT Luke Work.
Missouri returned five offensive starters from 2025 but lost six, including quarterback Beau Pribula, center Connor Tollison and tackle Keagen Trost.
Jamal Roberts is listed as the starting running back, followed by Xai'Shaun Edwards or Malae Fonoti.
Roberts rushed 13 times for 47 yards and a touchdown in the opener, moving him past 1,000 career rushing yards at Missouri.
Sophomore wide receiver Donovan Olugbode recorded career highs of seven receptions, 107 yards and two touchdowns in the opener.
Ole Miss transfer Cayden Lee is listed as a starting receiver and caught five passes for 89 yards, including a 47-yard touchdown, in his Missouri debut.

defensive_personnel.fact: Missouri returned only two defensive starters from 2025 and lost 10, including defensive linemen Chris McClellan and Zion Young, linebacker Josiah Trotter and cornerbacks Drey Norwood and Toriano Pride Jr.
Transfer linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. and transfer cornerback Chris Graves Jr. are listed as starters.
Woodyard started 11 games for Auburn in 2025 and recorded 67 tackles, including 50 in conference play.
Graves appeared in 41 games over three seasons at Ole Miss and started nine games in 2025.
Returning defensive tackles Marquis Gracial and Sterling Webb combined for 6.0 tackles for loss in 2025; Webb also recorded 2.5 sacks and six quarterback hurries.
Darris Smith, listed as the starting JACK edge defender, recorded four sacks in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Chip Lindsey joined Missouri as offensive coordinator in December 2025 and is in his first season in the role.
Garrett Riley joined Missouri in January 2026 as quarterbacks coach after serving as Clemson's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
John Papuchis became Missouri's special-teams coordinator and defensive assistant in January 2026 after six seasons coordinating special teams at Florida State.
Alex Atkins joined the staff in January 2026 as tight ends coach, and Chop Harbin joined as defensive line coach.
Linebackers coach Derek Nicholson added co-defensive coordinator duties before the 2026 season.

injury_availability.fact: The participation chart lists returning running back Ahmad Hardy with no appearances through Missouri's first game of 2026; the guide does not state a reason.
The participation chart lists starting left tackle Cayden Green with no appearance in the season opener; the guide does not state a reason.

offensive_context.fact: Missouri averaged 228.3 rushing yards per game in 2025, ranking eighth nationally and first in the SEC.
Missouri recorded a program-record 12 individual 100-yard rushing performances in 2025.
Missouri rushed for 31 touchdowns in 2025 and scored three rushing touchdowns in its 2026 opener.
In the 2026 opener, Missouri averaged 7.2 yards per play, converted 60% of its third downs and scored touchdowns on four of five red-zone possessions.

defensive_context.fact: Missouri's 2025 defense allowed 277.3 yards and 18.9 points per game, ranking eighth nationally in total defense and 17th in scoring defense.
The 2025 defense allowed 103.8 rushing yards and 173.5 passing yards per game.
Missouri held Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 198 total yards, 13 first downs and 3-of-13 third-down conversions in the 2026 opener.
Missouri's defense forced five three-and-outs against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Missouri did not force a turnover in the opener but recorded a safety and held Arkansas-Pine Bluff scoreless in the first half.

special_teams.fact: Blake Craig is listed as Missouri's starting placekicker, Brunno Reus as the starting punter and kickoff specialist, and Brett Le Blanc as the starting long snapper.
Craig made a 32-yard field goal and all seven extra-point attempts in the season opener.
Reus recorded a season-long 52-yard punt against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
DaMarion Fowlkes is listed as Missouri's primary punt and kickoff returner and had a 23-yard punt return in the opener.

other_relevant.fact: Missouri is scheduled to play at Mississippi State on Sept. 26, 2026 in its first SEC game of the season.
Missouri entered 2026 with nine returning starters: five on offense, two on defense and two on special teams.
Missouri is 30-10 since the beginning of the 2023 season.
